title: PrivateLB Terraform traffic orchestrator: internal multi-protocol listeners, TLS termination/passthrough, and health probe strategies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers deploying Redwood Private expect a predictable, internally routable ingress that supports mixed traffic (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC) and robust TLS handling. Current ad-hoc stacks we maintain have divergent Terraform patterns across customers and cause upgrade risk during model/runtime upgrades. Goal: Implement a single Terraform module (private_lb_orchestrator) that standardizes internal ingress patterns: NLB for TCP/gRPC passthrough, ALB for HTTP/HTTPS termination, unified target group healthcheck strategies, and built-in cert rotation hooks. The module must be upgrade-safe (no traffic blackholes during resource replacement), support cross-AZ target groups, provide connection-draining defaults, and expose observability hooks (CloudWatch/Prometheus labels).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module 'private_lb_orchestrator' added to infra-modules repo with versioned releases
Support for 3 listener modes: ALB-terminate-HTTPS, NLB-TLS-passthrough, and ALB-HTTP (redirect to HTTPS) via variables
Health check configuration parameters exposed: path, interval, healthy_threshold, unhealthy_threshold, timeout, protocol; defaults tuned for short-lived pods and long startup time services
Certificate rotation path integrated: optional ACM import or external cert-manager webhook; rotation does not require ALB replacement
Upgrade path documented with blue/green canary and stepdown sequence for target group swapping
Automated smoke test (terraform apply → deploy sample service → verify traffic routing and metrics) exists in CI
SLO metrics available: target group 5xx rate, latency p95, unhealthy host count — dashboards linked
Security review completed and module passes least-privilege IAM audit
tasks: Design API for module: inputs (vpc_id, subnet_ids, service_ports, certificate_arn, listener_mode, enable_stickiness) and outputs (alb_arn, nlb_dns, target_group_arns)
Implement ALB construct with two target groups (http and https) and automatic redirect rule from HTTP to HTTPS
Implement NLB listener option that preserves TLS to backend (TCP mode) and supports PROXY protocol for source IP preservation
Healthcheck policy implementation: support for HTTP path probe, TCP probe fallback, and GRPC healthcheck when enabled
Add lifecycle and create_before_destroy patterns for safe upgrades (target group replacement then listener switch)
Integrate certificate rotation flow: support for ACM ARN or webhook reference to customer cert-manager
Add variables and examples for cross-AZ target group balancing and stickiness configuration
Write comprehensive docs and upgrade guide (confluence) with rollback steps
Create CI terraform plan/apply smoke tests and integrate into shared pipeline
Coordinate security review and IAM policy least-privilege adjustments
comments: 2026-02-28: Marcus — Initial spike completed. Identified two upgrade risks: ALB listener replacement causes brief 5s outage if target replacement not sequenced; NLB TLS passthrough requires preserving client IP for logging. Recommend create_before_destroy on target groups plus a short overlap window for draining.

2026-03-03: PM Sara Liu — Prioritize cert rotation automation; a customer reported manual ACM swaps were error-prone during a recent private upgrade. Add a note to acceptance criteria for non-disruptive rotation.

2026-03-06: Design (Leo Ramos) — Proposed probe heuristics: default HTTP GET /_healthz with 3s timeout, 3/10 healthy/unhealthy; for gRPC use grpc_health_probe with startup probe of 60s. Shared doc linked below.

2026-03-10: Marcus — Implemented module skeleton and example; pushed draft PR for review (see links). Found Terraform AWS provider limitation with ALB rule priority collisions when many listeners are present — working around by deterministic priority allocation.
2026-03-12: Security (Nadia K.) — Quick review: require adding kms_key_id variable for access logs encryption and ensure ALB/NLB log buckets have lifecycle rules. Added to tasks.
notes: Tradeoffs: We can do TLS termination at the ALB for observability and WAF integration, but gRPC workloads benefit from TLS passthrough on NLB to avoid ALB HTTP/2 to backend translation issues.
Operational playbook will include commands for forcing draining, switching target groups, and reconstructing listeners in case of Terraform drift.
Plan B for provider limitations: if priority allocation edge cases persist, fall back to single ALB + path-based routing per-service documented in examples (higher latency for rule eval).
